title: JudgmentResolution
description: A standalone resolution record that captures the outcome of a judgment decision. This schema can be used independently from the full Judgment Point to represent resolution data in contexts such as audit logs, delegation records, and cross-system integrations. It extends the embedded resolution within a Judgment Point with additional fields that support accountability and bias-awareness.

selectedAlternativeId.description: Identifier of the chosen alternative from the Judgment Point's alternatives list.

rationale.description: Concise explanation of why this alternative was selected. Should be substantive enough for a reviewer to understand the reasoning without needing to reconstruct the original context.

uncertainty.description: Known uncertainties or unknowns at the time of resolution. Each entry describes a specific area where information was incomplete or where the outcome is not fully predictable.

conditions.description: Conditions or constraints applied to this resolution. These are specific requirements that bound how the resolution should be implemented (e.g., 'Use source data covering 300-900 K', 'Re-evaluate if sample size exceeds 10,000').

validationRequirements.description: Validation steps required after this resolution is applied. Each entry describes a check or test that must be performed to confirm the resolution produces acceptable results.

resolvedBy.description: Identifier of the person, agent, or policy that recorded this resolution.

resolutionType.description: How this resolution was produced. 'direct-human' means a human made the decision without AI input. 'collaborative' means a human decided after reviewing AI-generated analysis or recommendations. 'delegated' means an agent resolved under an explicit delegation policy. 'rule-based' means the resolution was determined by a predefined rule or standard. 'inherited' means the resolution was carried over from a prior decision on a materially similar Judgment Point.

informationPresented.description: Descriptions of what information was shown to the decision-maker before the resolution was recorded. This supports accountability by documenting the informational basis of the decision.

alternativesConsidered.description: Identifiers of all alternatives that were reviewed before making this resolution. Must include at least the selected alternative.

initialPosition.description: The decision-maker's stated position before seeing AI recommendations or structured comparison data. Capturing this supports detection of anchoring bias and ensures the record reflects independent judgment.

recommendationShown.description: Whether an AI-generated recommendation was displayed to the decision-maker before resolution. This field is critical for bias-awareness: when true, the resolution should be evaluated with awareness that the recommendation may have influenced the decision.
